metaDescription: Own mineral rights near Monroeville, AL, the Monroe County seat? Get a courthouse-verified, no-pressure offer from a direct buyer.
heroLead: Monroeville is the seat of Monroe County, which means the courthouse holding the deed and probate records for every family's mineral interest in the surrounding countryside sits right in town.
intro: Because Monroeville is the county seat, it's the natural starting point for tracing any mineral interest tied to Monroe County land, regardless of where within the county the actual tract sits. Families here have often held minerals for generations without much reason to think about them, since the leasing activity that has moved through this part of south Alabama has come in scattered waves rather than a single defining boom the way Citronelle shaped Mobile County.

sections.heading: The Courthouse at the Center of Everything
paragraphs: Every deed, probate file, and lease touching Monroe County land eventually runs through the Monroeville courthouse, which makes it the first stop in confirming any family's mineral title here. We do that research directly rather than relying on secondhand family recollection of who owns what.

sections.heading: Scattered Leasing, Not a Single Boom
paragraphs: Monroe County's oil and gas history is a patchwork of exploratory leasing from different decades rather than one dominant field, which means two neighboring Monroeville-area tracts can have very different histories. We look at your specific parcel's record rather than assuming based on the broader county.

faqs.question: Does living in the county seat make our own title research any different?
faqs.answer: Not fundamentally — we research your specific tract's history the same way regardless of where in the county it sits, though the records themselves are close by in Monroeville.

faqs.question: Our neighbor's land is producing but ours has never been leased. Why the difference?
faqs.answer: Monroe County's leasing history is scattered rather than uniform, so it's common for neighboring tracts to have very different histories. We check yours specifically.

faqs.question: How do we start if we're not sure exactly what our family owns?
faqs.answer: Send us whatever you have — an old deed, a probate file, even just a family name — and we'll research the Monroeville courthouse record from there.

faqs.question: Is it worth pursuing an interest with no clear royalty history?
faqs.answer: Often, yes. We look at your tract's leasing history and nearby activity rather than assuming a lack of royalty checks means no value at all.

faqs.question: Do you work with families who live outside Alabama but hold Monroe County minerals?
faqs.answer: Yes, most of our research and paperwork can be handled remotely regardless of where your family currently lives.
